prompt: What does Google Play call the part of the store page where an app's data practices are shown?

choices.text: Privacy Nutrition Labels
choices.why: That is Apple's description of its own labels.

choices.text: The privacy manifest
choices.why: The manifest is a file inside an iOS app, not a section of the Play page.

choices.text: Data safety
choices.why: Right, filled in on the App content page of the Play Console.

choices.text: App Tracking Transparency
choices.why: That is Apple's framework for asking to track.

prompt: By Apple's definition, which of these is collected?

choices.text: One email address sent to your server and kept there
choices.why: Right. It left the device and is kept longer than the request needed.

choices.text: Four thousand study sessions stored on the phone
choices.why: Data that stays on the device is not collected, however much there is.

choices.text: A reminder time the phone uses to schedule a notification
choices.why: It never leaves the phone.

choices.text: A course title shown on the screen
choices.why: Showing data is not sending it anywhere.

prompt: A team adds an analytics SDK and does not change its Data safety answers, because "we did not write that code". Who is responsible for the form being accurate?

choices.text: The SDK's company
choices.why: Android's guide says the developer alone is responsible, SDKs included.

choices.text: Google, which reviews every app
choices.why: Google says it cannot make those determinations on the developer's behalf.

choices.text: Nobody, until a user complains
choices.why: Google may take enforcement action when it finds a discrepancy.

choices.text: The team
choices.why: Right. A library's collection is the app's collection on the form.

prompt: Data is collected only to make the app work. On Apple's form, what happens to it?

choices.text: It is left out, since it is not analytics or advertising
choices.why: Apple's page says it still needs to be declared.

choices.text: It is declared, with App Functionality as its purpose
choices.why: Right. A purpose describes a collection; it does not excuse it.

choices.text: It is declared as tracking
choices.why: Tracking is linking with other companies' data for ads, or a data broker.

choices.text: It goes in the privacy manifest only
choices.why: The form and the manifest both describe it.

prompt: Which of these count as tracking, in Apple's definition? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: linking your app's data with other companies' data for targeted ads
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: passing data about a user to a data broker
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: counting how many people open the week screen, in your own app
choices.why: That is analytics: collection to declare, but not tracking.

choices.text: keeping the study plan on the phone
choices.why: Nothing leaves the device.

prompt: In both forms, data that a library inside your app sends to another company counts as collected and ___.
What is the file name of an iOS privacy manifest?

choices.text: Info.plist
choices.why: Info.plist holds the purpose strings of lesson 12.

choices.text: PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy
choices.why: Right, a property list inside the app and inside each SDK.

choices.text: apple-app-site-association
choices.why: That is the website's file for universal links.

choices.text: assetlinks.json
choices.why: That is Android's file for App Links.

prompt: Why does Apple ask for a reason before an app may read something as ordinary as the free disk space?

choices.text: Reading the disk is slow
choices.why: Speed is not the concern; identification is.

choices.text: Because disk space is personal data
choices.why: It is not personal; it is a signal that helps tell devices apart.

choices.text: Because the person has to grant a permission first
choices.why: No dialog is involved; the reason is declared in the manifest.

choices.text: It helps identify a device: fingerprinting
choices.why: Right: combined with other signals. Fingerprinting is not allowed whatever the person said about tracking.

prompt: Match each key of the planner's privacy manifest to what its value says.

pairs.right: user defaults, for the app's own data

right_distractors: the domains it sends analytics to

prompt: An app's own manifest is perfect, and it adds an SDK whose manifest declares a tracking domain. The person refuses tracking. What happens to the SDK's requests to that domain?

choices.text: They fail
choices.why: Right. Apple's documentation says requests to tracking domains fail without tracking permission.

choices.text: They go through, because the app's manifest says it does not track
choices.why: Each manifest speaks for its own code; the app's does not cover the SDK.

choices.text: They are delayed until the person changes their mind
choices.why: Nothing waits; the requests fail.

choices.text: The app is removed from the store
choices.why: Refusing tracking is the person's right, not a violation.

prompt: What must an iOS app add before it shows the App Tracking Transparency request?

choices.text: An entry in assetlinks.json
choices.why: That is Android's file for links.

choices.text: A Data safety form
choices.why: That is Google Play's.

choices.text: An NSUserTrackingUsageDescription purpose string
choices.why: Right, like the purpose strings of lesson 12.

choices.text: A required reason code such as CA92.1
choices.why: That code is for user defaults, not tracking.

prompt: In declare.ts, how many kinds of data does the inventory with two SDKs list?
The planner's own inventory has three entries. Why does declare print "collected: nothing"?

choices.text: All three stay on the device
choices.why: Right. Only what leaves the device is collected.

choices.text: Because App Functionality does not need declaring
choices.why: It does, when the data leaves the device.

choices.text: Because reminder times are optional
choices.why: Optional data that leaves the device is still collected.

choices.text: Because the planner has no server yet, so nothing counts until it does
choices.why: A third-party SDK would collect without any server of the planner's.

prompt: The careless inventory has why: "". Why did TypeScript not stop it?

choices.text: Because why is optional in the Item type
choices.why: It is required: why: string.

choices.text: Because the entry is optional: true
choices.why: optional is about the student, not about the type.

choices.text: An empty string is a string, and node strips types without checking them
choices.why: Right. That is why check runs when the program runs.

choices.text: Because declare.ts has a type error that node ignores at the end
choices.why: There is no type error: "" is a valid string.

prompt: A team moves the planner's sessions to its own server for syncing, and changes nothing else. What does declare now print for sessions?

choices.text: collected: nothing, because the server is the team's own
choices.why: Your own server is off the device: that is collection.

choices.text: Collected, App Functionality, not shared, required
choices.why: Right. It left the device but reached no third party.

choices.text: Collected and shared, because a server is a third party
choices.why: Only another company's server makes it shared.

choices.text: A refusal, because sessions have no reason
choices.why: They keep their reason; only where they go changed.

prompt: Match where data goes to what the form says about it.
right_distractors: exempt, since an SDK sent it

prompt: Which of these does the planner need?

choices.text: The student's location
choices.why: A study session has no place.

choices.text: An account with an email
choices.why: The plan lives on the phone.

choices.text: A device identifier for analytics
choices.why: Nothing the student sees depends on it.

choices.text: None of these
choices.why: Right. It needs no account, location, contacts or device identifier.

prompt: The planner wants crash reports. What does the lesson suggest starting from?

choices.text: A crash SDK, declared on both forms
choices.why: That is the expensive answer; there is a cheaper one first.

choices.text: Asking students to email screenshots whenever the app closes
choices.why: That collects more, not less.

choices.text: The reports the system gathers, shown in the stores' consoles
choices.why: Right. No SDK, so the form stays empty for as long as they are enough.

choices.text: Nothing; crashes do not matter
choices.why: They matter; the question is how to learn about them.

prompt: Why does the lesson treat a device identifier as costly when it is only a few bytes?

choices.text: It ties every screen opened to one phone
choices.why: Right, and that cannot be undone: removing what links data to a person works only before collection.

choices.text: Because the stores charge for each identifier
choices.why: No store charges for it.

choices.text: Because it slows the app
choices.why: The cost is not performance.

choices.text: Because Android forbids it
choices.why: The lesson's argument is about the person, not a rule.

prompt: Put the questions in the order the lesson asks them about a new kind of data.
items: is it worth collecting at all?
what is the reason, in a sentence?

prompt: Why is ?from=email not in the planner's inventory?

choices.text: Because query strings are not data
choices.why: It is data about where a person came from.

choices.text: Because lesson 11 refused that link
choices.why: Lesson 11 opened it, ignoring the query.

choices.text: Because the stores exempt marketing tags
choices.why: No such exemption is described.

choices.text: The planner reads it for nothing and sends it nowhere
choices.why: Right. If it ever counted installs by source, that would be a new line with a reason.

prompt: A team says their label is fine because they only use an analytics SDK "for functionality". What is wrong with the reasoning?

choices.text: Nothing; functionality is exempt
choices.why: Apple's page says functionality data still has to be declared.

choices.text: The SDK's collection is theirs to declare, whatever the purpose
choices.why: Right. A purpose describes a collection; it does not remove it.

choices.text: Analytics is always tracking
choices.why: Tracking is a narrower thing; analytics of your own app is not tracking.

choices.text: SDKs are not allowed on iOS
choices.why: They are allowed, with their own manifests.

prompt: For the inventory with two SDKs, how many lines starting with collected: did declare print?
Which of these makes a privacy statement a person does not have to trust anybody to keep?

choices.text: A long privacy policy
choices.why: A policy is a promise somebody has to keep.

choices.text: Keeping the data on the device
choices.why: Right. Nothing collected is nothing anybody can mishandle.

choices.text: Encrypting data on your server
choices.why: The data still left the phone, and the server still holds it.

choices.text: Asking for tracking permission politely
choices.why: Asking nicely still collects.
